mstts:express-as.prosody: Ever notice how, just when you’re ready to dive into something creative, something invisible seems to get in the way? Maybe it’s doubt, procrastination, or just that nagging voice telling you to wait until tomorrow. That’s exactly the heart of what Steven Pressfield explores in his powerful book, The War of Art. We’re about to step into the real struggle that anyone chasing a dream faces—the inner pushback that shows up when you try to write, start a business, or simply live a life that feels true to you. It’s wild how the toughest obstacles aren’t always out there in the world, but right inside our own minds. Fear, hesitation, even self-sabotage—they’re all part of the creative battleground. But here’s where it gets interesting: Pressfield doesn’t just name these barriers, he helps us spot them, understand them, and, most importantly, fight back. We’ll be talking about what it really means to move from dabbling like an amateur to showing up each day as a professional—no matter what your craft is. Along the way, we’ll discover how discipline and perseverance aren’t just nice-to-haves—they’re the essential tools to unlock your creativity and reach that sense of fulfillment you’ve been searching for. So, as we travel together through the lessons of The War of Art, let’s get curious about what’s holding us back… and even more excited about the possibility of finally breaking through. Ready to take the first step? Let’s dive in.
